section_summary.extract_value: This conclusion section emphasizes the importance of body appreciation as a modifiable factor for promoting resilience and well-being in women. It suggests that clinical interventions should focus on helping women appreciate their bodies rather than changing their appearance. The text refers to "the present study" implying a single study, and hopes it will encourage further research into body appreciation-centered interventions.
section_summary.evidence_source: Conclusion It is well established that an important role of psychology research is to identify variables that can be modified through intervention in order to promote resilience and well-being (e.g., Resnick, 2000). In line with the resiliency paradigm, we propose that body appreciation is one such factor amenable to intervention, which could contribute to ameliorate women's relationship to their body. Derailing the observable effects of age or helping a person profoundly change their appearance can be quite a challenging feat. It may be unlikely that women who have experienced years of shame and dislike for their body will concede to becoming satisfied with the way they look. Rather, a more realistic and potentially effective avenue for clinical intervention may be helping women to appreciate their body for what it is and for what it can do. In this regard, it is hoped that the present study will spur further research to eventually assist in the development of body appreciationcentered interventions, emphasizing its intricate role in sexual health.
